speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Invariant eigendistributions and the first descent construction
summary: The first lecture on Harish-Chandra begins after the programme on P000187. It states local integrability and regular-set analyticity for conjugation-invariant, centrally finite distributions, then sketches ellipticity, descent through centralizers, and reduction near the identity to the Lie algebra. Gelfand supplies explicit central operators for the general linear group. The lecture ends on P000191 before Dynin's heading. Several compressed proof steps need correction; the unexplained sentence about characters at infinity is retained as unidentified.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Pseudodifferential operators on bundles and the de Rham example
summary: Dynin begins after Kirillov on P000191, globalizing pseudodifferential operators by coordinate cutoffs and the off-diagonal smoothing condition. The only worked example is the operator \(d+d^*\), its Laplacian, and the Hodge identification with de Rham cohomology. The final timetable is administrative, not another mathematical result.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Enveloping-algebra construction of radial differential operators
summary: The second Harish-Chandra lecture constructs \(\Gamma_y\), transferring differentiation in the conjugating variable to the section. Its associated-graded calculation yields a PBW decomposition and the constant transverse term defining the radial operator. The first part of P000195 still belongs to this lecture; the dated 27 February heading starts record 122.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Distributional descent and the induction step for regularity
summary: The third lecture returns to continuous fiber integration, pulls an invariant distribution back to \(G\times\Xi'\), and factors it as Haar measure times a distribution on the centralizer. It states intertwining with radial differential operators and finite central codimension, thereby reducing local integrability to a smaller group. The notebook itself rejects an attempted explicit inverse-substitution formula.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: The Lorentzian rank-one model for invariant regularity
summary: A short final Kirillov note isolates the form \(x^2+y^2-z^2\), its wave operator, and invariant distributions annihilated by a polynomial in that operator. The question of local summability is the rank-one Lie-algebra case of the theorem developed in the preceding lectures. Arnold's report begins later on the same page.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Surface diffeomorphism groups; adjacent Anosov note on operator Fourier transformation
summary: Arnold reports Earle--Eells on the topology of the identity component of the diffeomorphism group of an oriented surface, with genus-by-genus answers and the quasiconformal proof strategy. P000199 begins a distinct, explicit \ru{Аносов} heading and develops an operator-valued Fourier transform attributed to Maslov. The catalogue supplies no separate record for this subsection; its three items are retained here with Anosov as the item-level speaker. This grouping preserves source coverage without attributing Anosov's mathematics to Arnold.

speaker: A. N. Parshin
title: Algebraic group actions and geometric orbit quotients
summary: Parshin's report on Mumford defines a regular algebraic action and asks when its orbit set carries an algebraic quotient structure. It records stabilizer semicontinuity, necessary restrictions on a morphism whose fibers are individual orbits, and the affine reductive closed-orbit criterion in compressed form. An unlabelled hyperbola-like sketch cannot be uniquely identified. The later projective continuation, record 128, preserves only a heading.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Stable symbols and an axiomatic index
summary: Dynin's second lecture defines compactly supported stable symbols and lists homotopy invariance, additivity, products, excision, vanishing for symbols from the base, and the one-dimensional winding normalization. The first isolated uniqueness claim mentions only the first two properties and is false literally; the later full family of axioms supplies the intended setting. This is related to the earlier index lectures, but no already-indexed open question is reasserted.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Boundary systems with varying partial indices and global completion
summary: The March 27 material begins below the separate March 20 Parshin heading on P000202. The catalogue attributes this record to Dynin, but the manuscript names Eskin on P000203; this could introduce Eskin's work or a further speaker, and the catalogue attribution is retained with that qualification. The lecture treats a continuous family of normal half-line problems even when individual partial indices jump, auxiliary potentials and boundary equations, localization, and a global completion question. The latter matches the framework and criterion of Vishik--Eskin's paper received 27 April 1967, rather than merely a later paper on the same subject.

speaker: A. N. Parshin
title: Projective varieties: heading of the continued Mumford report
summary: Only the handwritten date 20 March and the headings ``Continuation of Parshin's report'' and ``The case of projective varieties'' survive. The next visible mathematics is below a new date, 27 March, and concerns matrix factorization; it belongs to record 127. No theorem from Mumford's projective invariant theory is supplied by this heading. Catalogue source order is preserved even though record 128 has the earlier date.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Petrovsky lacunas and Atiyah’s algebraic-geometric formulation
summary: S. Gelfand explicitly reports Atiyah's Bourbaki expos\'e 319, delivered in February 1967 and printed in 1968. The notes define strict hyperbolicity, the retarded fundamental solution and stable lacunas, construct the two Petrovsky homology classes, state the even-order/even-dimension criteria, and begin the residue-integral proof. The shift from \(\mathbb R^n\) to coordinates \(x_0,\ldots,x_n\) is resolved by writing \(N=n+1\). Empty real and complex sections, projective orientation choices, and twisted canonical forms must be distinguished. The notes stop at the Herglotz--Petrovsky formula; later algebraic de Rham proof details are not attributed to the seminar.
